title: Quiet PR refinery scratchpad
content:
Purpose
---
A low-noise scratchpad for shaping small PRs and micro-refactors that touch hot paths. Focus: reduce churn, keep canaries tiny, make rollbacks simple, and capture minimal verification steps so reviewers can be fast and confident.

High-level heuristics (mental model)
- Aim for atomic commits that are both build-and-test green locally and have an obvious rollback commit.
- Prefer a runtime-safe flag or config toggle over invasive migrations when user-visible behavior changes are possible.
- Small perf regressions are OK if guarded by thresholds and a short canary window.
- Document the cost/risk tradeoff up front (token cost, latency delta, SLO exposure).

Quick checklist (pre-PR)
- [ ] Rebase onto latest main and smoke-run unit tests.
- [ ] Run small local perf harness (scripts/perf/local_bench.sh) for the hot code paths changed. Capture output (latency p50/p95, mem).
- [ ] Confirm KV cache interactions: will this change invalidate prefixes or change cache keys? If yes, add compatibility layer or migration notes.
- [ ] Add a short snippet to CHANGELOG-UNRELEASED.md describing runtime impact in 1-2 sentences.
- [ ] Add a feature flag gate (env var + config) for any nontrivial behavior change.
- [ ] Add a unit/integration test that exercises the new code path end-to-end (mocking KV if needed).
- [ ] Outline a 1-step rollback in PR description.

Reviewer guidance (copy into PR description)
- What to look for: correctness, non-blocking regressions, and obvious rollback.
- Perf: compare p50/p95 from perf harness (attach output). If no harness, ask dev to provide one-liner to reproduce locally.
- Safety: does this touch cache keys, serialization formats, or logging/metrics names? If yes, require compatibility notes.
- Observability: new metrics or tags? Ensure they follow naming conventions and have dashboards/alerts planned.

Canary plan template (if > trivial change)
1) Deploy behind feature flag to 1% of traffic (route policy: region=us-west).
2) Monitor p50/p95, error_rate, token_cost_per_request for 30 min.
3) If regressions > thresholds (error_rate +0.1%, p95 +15%) then flip flag off and revert.
4) If stable for 24h, expand to 20% then 100% with 1h windows.

Rollback options (ordered)
- Flip feature flag (fastest).
- Revert PR and deploy (requires release cycle).
- Apply mitigation patch that isolates change (e.g., short-circuit path).

Mini decision record (to paste in PR)
- Decision: Keep existing KV key composition; add versioned prefix 'v2' for this refactor so we can co-exist during rollout.
- Reasoning: Avoid full cache invalidation; allows canary to warm new keys without impacting global cache hit rate.
- Risk: Increased memory for duplicated cache entries for the warm-up window (estimate ~2-5% depending on traffic).

Refactor map (small follow-ups)
- Split long function inference_runner.handle_request() into 3 focused helpers: validate_inputs, route_model, stream_response. Each helper should be <120 LOC.
- Replace ad-hoc timing logs with metrics.timer('inference.handle_request_ms') to enable p50/p95 alerting.
- Inline short-lived feature flags into a single config struct to reduce conditional branching.

Testing recipes (local)
- unit: tox -e py39 -- tests/unit/test_runner.py::test_prefix_handling
- integration: ./scripts/run_local_integration.sh --model gpt-small --input tests/fixtures/sample_prompt.json
- perf: ./scripts/perf/local_bench.sh --concurrency 8 --seq-len 256 --iters 200 | tee /tmp/pr-perf.out
- cache correctness: python -c "from kvclient import Client; c=Client(); c.set('k','v'); assert c.get('k')=='v'"

Open questions / quick TODOs (notes to self)
- Q1: How will this interact with dedicated/pinned model variants? (ask @Noelle)
- Q2: Does the logging volume spike when we add new metrics tags? Need to estimate S3/ES ingest delta. (ask infra)
- TODO: Add a test that simulates cache warm-up and confirms concurrent requests still hit new key after warm. (owner: Arjun)
- TODO: Draft small dashboard widget showing token_cost_per_request across canary groups. (owner: Tamsin)

Slack + tickets to mention in PR
- slack: #serving-runtime thread "perf spike from kv-prefix-change" (link placeholder)
- jira: INF-889 (refactor grooming notes)
- gh: PR #4721 (perf helper and small refactor)

Notes to self (style + etiquette)
- Keep PR description short but explicit about runtime exposure and rollback path. Reviewers skim for rollback/metrics.
- Use small commits with meaningful messages; reviewers can squash later, but commit granularity helps bisect if we need to revert.
- If reviewer requests a big design change, respond with a short proposal and split the work: immediate safety fix vs larger redesign.

Last-minute checklist before merge
- [ ] PR description has perf numbers + canary plan + rollback step.
- [ ] Tests passing in CI and a green integration run on staging.
- [ ] Add reviewer note: "OK to merge once metric x stays within threshold for 30m".

Fragments (copy/paste snippets)
- PR description header snippet:
  "Summary: small refactor to route selection that introduces a v2 cache prefix. Canary plan: 1% traffic us-west for 30m. Rollback: flip FEATURE_X to false. Perf: see attached /tmp/pr-perf.out."

- Revert commit template:
  "revert: <original commit subject>

  This reverts commit <sha> which introduced <brief reason>. Revert triggered by <reason> and observed at <time>."

End notes
- Keep this doc short-lived; once a pattern matures, move distilled bits to CONFLUENCE:Refactor-Guidelines and remove from personal scratchpad.
- If this PR grows beyond two files or touches >3 subsystems, escalate to design review meeting.

Random: morning thought: a "safety lint" pre-commit that warns when a PR changes metric names, serialization formats, or cache keys might save cycles. Prototype idea: parse diffs for strings matching /cache_key_|metric_|log_tag_/ and prompt author to add migration notes.
